newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria to call tender for gas storage expansion.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria to call tender for gas storage expansion.

text.p: Bulgaria plans to call a tender in a bid to seek foreign investment to expand capacity at its Chiren natural gas storage facility, officials from the state-owned gas monopolist Bulgargas said on Wednesday.
"Western firms and (Bulgarian-Russian joint gas stock company) Topenergy have shown interest in participating with investments," a Bulgargas official, who declined to be named, told Reuters.

France's Gaz de France is among the companies to have shown interest in the expansion, in which Bulgargas has already pumped 57 million levs, officials said. Chiren's current capacity is 2.5 million cubic metres per day.

The underground Chiren facility in northern Bulgaria, which has been operating for 22 years, would be expanded in several stages, increasing annual capacity to 3-4 billion cubic metres from almost one billion currently.

Bulgargas officials said Turkey's state run pipeline company Botas and Topenergy had shown interest in the construction of a new underground storage facility using abandoned salt caverns in the village of Mirovo near the industrial area of Devnya in northeastern Bulgaria.
For the last nine years a gas pipeline has linked Bulgaria with Turkey, which expects to increase its Russian gas imports via Bulgaria to about 20 billion cubic metres annually in the next few years.
A gas storage facility at Mirovo with a provisional capacity of 300-500 million cubic metres would help Turkey to overcome sharp falls in Russian gas supplies in cold winters.
Topenergy, in which Russia's gas giant Gazprom holds a 50 percent stake, plans to sell and deliver Russian gas to the Balkans via Bulgaria.

Bulgaria has a 2,200-km pipeline network including 625 km of transit pipelines, receiving and transmitting gas from outside the country, which may become a transit gas corridor from Russia to the Balkans and Italy.
